sentences.text: THE MFA AND MFA.CROB, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, UMESH M. ADIGA. J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT The Insurer in M.V.C.No.1105/2021 has filed this appeal M.F.A.No.200767/2023 challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and the claimants have filed cross-objections in M.F.A.No.200049/2023 claiming for enhancement of compensation in the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi dated 12.12.2022 (for short, hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
2.
The matters are slated for hearing on admission.
With the consent of both the sides, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. It is the case of the claimant that on 27.11.2020, deceased Sagar along with his friends were traveling in Car bearing Reg.No.KA-32/N-6900 on Humnabad-Kalaburagi road.
The driver of the said car was driving the said vehicle in a rash and neglient manner.

Due to the same, it met with NC:
2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 an accident at 4.30 a.m. causing grievous injuries to the said Sagar.
He was shifted to Vatsalya Life Hospital, Kalaburag,i wherein the Doctor declared that he was brought dead.
4. The claimants are parents of the deceased Sagar.
They have contended that deceased was aged 32 years and he was Contractor, earning Rs.5 to 6 Lakhs per annum.
Claimant No.2 is father of the deceased and he is physically handicapped.
Both the claimants were depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.71,60,000/-.

5. The Insurer has contended that owner of the vehicle had violated terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance and it denied all the petition averments and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
6.
From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.

7. the claimants have examined PW-1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P16.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 8.

The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating pleadings and evidence on record,
awarded the following compensation:
 Sl.No.

Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 49,28,000  2. Loss of consortium 80,000  3. Funeral expenses 15,000  4. Loss of estate 15,000 Laxmi @ Laxmibai vs The Divisional Manager And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37563047/
4

sentences.text:
The Tribunal has taken income of the deceased as Rs.6,16,000/-, deducted 50% of the said amount towards personal expenses, added 40% of future prospects of his income, applied multiplier as '16' and awarded the compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.
10.
We have heard the arguments of the learned Advocates on both sides.
11. The learned Advocate for the Appellant/Insurer has submitted that the Tribunal has relied on Exs.P7 to P9 and taken income of the deceased at Rs.3,08,000/- per annum, which is on the higher side.

Except the said Income- tax returns, no other materials are placed on record to prove NC:
2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 the income.
Moreover, the Income-tax returns were submitted just about six months prior to the death of Sagar.
Hence, it cannot be relied.
The Tribunal has erred in adding 40% of the amount towards future prospects.
Therefore, prayed to re-calculate the compensation.
12. The learned Advocate for the Respondent- Claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has not taken the income of the deceased properly.
It is the case of the claimants that claimant No.2 is suffering from permanent disability and he is physically handicapped.
He is unable to earn any income.
Therefore, the liability on the deceased to look after both the claimants.
The Tribunal ought to have deducted 1/3rd of his income towards his personal expenses instead of 50%.
With these reasons, prayed to re-calculate the income and award just compensation.

13. The following points emerges for our determination:
"Whether the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation?"
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 14.
Fact of accident and death of Sagar due to accident is not in dispute.
Deceased was aged 32 years is also not in dispute.
The Insurer is seriously disputing the income of the deceased.
15. Claimants have produced Income-tax returns acknowledgement for the assessment year 2018-2019, 2019- 2020 and 2020-2021 at Exs.P7 to P9.
Exs. P7 and P8 were submitted on 27.06.2020.
Therefore, it is difficult to accept the submission of the learned advocate for the appellant that he said Income-tax returns were created for the purpose of claiming higher compensation.
Admittedly, accident had taken place on 28.11.2020.
The deceased even might not have dreamt that he would die in an accident within six months from date of filing of returns.
Under these circumstances, Exs.P7 to P9 are acceptable.
16. The Tribunal while taking the income of the deceased on the basis of Exs.P7 to P9, has not deducted the Income-tax paid by the deceased/assessee.
Therefore, it needs to be deducted from the said income.

The Tribunal has rightly added 40% of the said income towards future prospects since age of the deceased is below 40 years.
18. The submission of the learned advocate for the claimants that claimant No.2 is not earning member in the family.
He is suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 70% as per Ex.P15.
In view of the same, entire burden was on the deceased to look after the parents.
Under these circumstances, 1/3rd of his income could be - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 deducted as personal expenses.
The learned advocate of the Insurer has submitted that the said submission of the learned Advocate for the claimant is not tenable.

Time and again from the case of SARLA VERMA VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION1 to the Constitutional Bench judgment in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS2, it is held that when a bachelor dies, in the vehicle accident, 50% of his income is to be deducted towards personal expenses.

sentences.text: Therefore, in all the probability, the claimants might have their own source of income and from the said source of income, they brought him up and educated the deceased.
Claimants might have financed the deceased to start up the business.

Therefore, the submission of the claimant that they were completely 1 (2009) 6 SCC 121 2 2017 ACJ 2700 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 depending upon the earning of the deceased and claimants had no independent source of income is not acceptable.
19. The submission of the learned Advocate for the Insurer is tenable.
Claimants have not made out any case stating that someone has contributed for survival of the claimants as well as the deceased and educated him.
Under such circumstances, claimants might be having their own source of income to look after themselves as well as to maintain the deceased and educate him.

Admittedly,
the deceased was unmarried.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 50% of the earning of the deceased towards personal expenses.
The multiplier applicable in this case is admittedly '16' since deceased was aged about 32 years.

Hence, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is:
Income of deceased Rs.4,71,646/-
 Add 40% of future  prospects Rs.1,88,658/-
 Rs.6,60,304/-
 Less 50% of personal  expenses Rs.3,30,152/-
 Total 3,30,152X16  (multiplier) =
 Rs.52,82,43/-
 - 12 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB  C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 20.

It is not in dispute that the Tribunal has awarded compensation for loss of consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estate in accordance with the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra) and there is no need of re-considering the same.

The claimants are entitled for following amount of compensation:
 Sl.No. Particulars Amount  (Rs.)

7  3. Funeral expenses 15,000  4. Loss of estate 15,000

ORDER
The Appeal in M.F.A.No.200767 of 2023 is dismissed.
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 The Appeal in MFA.CROB No.200049 of 2023 is partly allowed.

The impugned judgment and award passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi in M.V.C.No.1105/2021 dated 12.12.2022 is modified as under:
a) The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.53,92,432 (Rupees Fifty Three Lakhs Ninety Two Thousand Four Hundred and Thirty Two only) as against Rs.50,38,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal and they are entitled for enhancement of Rs.3,54,432/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty Four Thousand Four Hundred and Thirty Two only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount from the date of the petition till its payment.
b) Respondent No.2 shall deposit the said enhanced amount with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the award.
- 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5962-DB C/W MFA.CROB No. 200049 of 2023 c) The orders of the Tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release are not interfered with.
The amount of compensation deposited by the Insurer in M.F.A.No.200767/2023 shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for releasing the amount in favour of the claimants.
